nodes.body: You stop here for a while to look around at the new place you have come to, and you wait a bit before you go on.
You are sailing your little boat when black clouds roll in fast. The wind howls and the sea turns the color of iron. Do you try to turn back to shore, or ride out the storm where you are?

You spin the tiller hard, but a wave slams the boat sideways and knocks you into the freezing water. Nobody on shore can see you out here. Do you fire the flare from your vest pocket, or try to stay afloat?
The flare goes up red against the black clouds. Soon a harbour boat swings toward you with its searchlight on, and strong hands haul you out of the water.
You grip the mast as the boat is thrown up and over a huge wave, then it flips, dumping you into the churning dark sea. Do you blow the whistle clipped to your vest, or try to stay afloat?
You blow until your chest aches. A fishing crew hears it through the wind and comes about. You learn something you will not forget: the whistle was the most useful thing on the whole boat.

The water is cold and black, and you cannot see the shore anymore. Your arms are getting tired, and no one is coming. Do you keep swimming toward where you think land is, or hold onto a floating plank and wait?
After what feels like forever, your fingers hit something solid: the hull of a fishing boat. Strong hands pull you aboard. You are shaking, cold, and alive.
You cling to the plank until, hours later, the storm passes and a coast guard boat finds you, half-frozen but breathing.
